original.guitar: Stéphane Dufour is Éric Lapointe's longtime guitarist; the credits for this track were not found
original.amp: Not documented. Mid-90s rock: Marshall-style crunch
original.effects: Delay, room reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Breakthrough single from Obsession (1994), produced by Aldo Nova. Also titled "Terre promise (poussé par le vent)".

recipes.tips: Channel A is an AC30 crunch for the verses: roll the guitar volume back to 7 for a cleaner sound. Channel B is a JCM900-style crunch for the big choruses. For the solo, switch to TERRE SO.
recipes.why: Mid-90s Quebec rock relied on crunchy Marshall-style guitars with a tight low end. The AC30 keeps the verses open, and the JCM900-style amp gives the choruses weight. A quiet delay and a small room keep it punchy under the vocals.

sources.title: SOCAN Magazine: SOCAN Classics, N'importe quoi, Terre promise, Poussé par le vent, Marie Stone (1994)

original.guitar: Stéphane Dufour is Éric Lapointe's longtime guitarist; the credits for this track were not found
original.amp: Not documented. Mid-90s rock lead: Marshall-style amp pushed by an overdrive
original.effects: Overdrive, stereo delay, hall reverb (era style, not documented)
original.notes: Breakthrough single from Obsession (1994), produced by Aldo Nova.

recipes.tips: Loads on channel B, ready for the solo. Channel A is a bit less gain for lead lines and fills. The stereo delay ducks under your playing and fills the gaps between phrases. Wide vibrato and long bends suit the style.
recipes.why: A JCM900-style amp pushed by a light overdrive gives a thick, sustained 90s rock lead. A long stereo delay and a hall reverb give the solo space.

sources.title: SOCAN Magazine: SOCAN Classics, N'importe quoi, Terre promise, Poussé par le vent, Marie Stone (1994)
